name: Faraquet
label: Dischord
lede: Faraquet played so few shows in its first life that the 2025 comeback sold out Tokyo twice. In between came one album of odd meters and melody, a tour with Fugazi, and a trip to Brazil.

eras.title: A side project outlives its host
eras.text: Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter had been playing together since they were about eighteen. In DC, Ocampo landed behind the drum kit in Smart Went Crazy, met Jeff Boswell there, and started something on the side that turned out to be the main event.

years.h: Faraquet starts out of Smart Went Crazy
years.p: [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] moves to guitar and vocals, [[Chad Molter|794c2243-0136-4627-887c-00749b81475d]] takes the drums and Jeff Boswell picks up bass. Dischord dates the start to June 1997; when [[Smart Went Crazy|d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2]] folds, Faraquet goes full-time.
years.xp:
Ocampo and Molter were old friends who moved to Washington to make music. It was [[Travis Morrison|b9ba9319-c5c7-4316-b32a-d3f92a673e1f]] of [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]] who connected Ocampo with Smart Went Crazy, where he drummed and met Boswell.

The influences weren't the usual DC ones: [[King Crimson|b38225b8-8e5f-42aa-bcdc-7bae5b5bdab3]] and Yes alongside [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]] Ocampo also told Exclaim! he takes a lot of influence from jazz horn players instead of guitar players. People called it math rock. He thought that was a simple term.

years.h: Parakeet and Um Die Ecke make Faraquet's first 7"
years.p: The single comes out on Mis En Scene. Dischord later gathers it onto Anthology 1997–98.

eras.title: One tower, then silence
eras.text: Two more singles, a tour with Fugazi, and The View From This Tower, cut with J. Robbins at Inner Ear. Then, with barely a week of shows behind the album, Ocampo, Molter and Boswell decided they were done.

yt: Live at the Black Cat Backstage, Nov 28, 1999
years.h: The Whole Thing Over and Call It Sane land on DeSoto
years.p: That 7" comes out on DeSoto Records, and Faraquet also splits a single with [[Akarso|5c6a66e2-d8d7-46a1-a1f2-b19f9fea2c85]] on 404 Records.

years.h: Live at the Black Cat Backstage, November 28, 1999
yt: Live at the Black Cat Backstage, November 28, 1999

years.p: Dischord's history says [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] invited Faraquet along, and after the tour the band went into the studio for its first album.

yt: Yo-Yo live at the Black Cat, circa 2000
years.h: Nine songs at Inner Ear become The View From This Tower
years.p: Dischord No. 122 is Faraquet's only studio album, co-produced by [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]]. Cut Self Not, Carefully Planned and Study in Complacency are among the nine.

years.big: We were at a creative standstill
q: and it just felt like it was at the end of things.
years.h: Four years in, Faraquet calls it
years.p: One album later, Ocampo tells Exclaim!, the band ends.
years.xp:
Faraquet lasted about four years and put out one album. By Ocampo's count they "really only played a week of shows" after it came out. There was no blowup on the record, just a band that had run out of road together.

Ocampo and Molter kept going as [[Medications|c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce]], which made an EP and two albums for Dischord. Ocampo went on to work as an engineer and producer at Inner Ear.

eras.title: Brazil first, then home
eras.text: Fans kept asking for Faraquet's out-of-print singles. Gathering them up gave the band an excuse to play again, starting a long way from D.C., in Brazil.

years.p: Announced in summer 2007, Dischord No. 159 collects Faraquet's singles and splits, plus one unreleased song and one outtake remixed by Ocampo. The LP comes on opaque yellow vinyl.
years.xp: Ten songs in all, mastered by [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] at Silver Sonya.

years.cap: Ocampo and Molter at Studio SP, Sao Paulo, September 2007
years.h: Brazil first, then all three play D.C. again
years.p: Ocampo and Molter play Brazil without Boswell in September 2007. Back in Washington the three of them reunite to mark Anthology 1997–98, as promised.
years.xp:
Ocampo told Exclaim! it was "not a reunion so we can make money or do anything other than play and have fun."

The Brazil dates included Studio SP and Centro Cultural Jabaquara in Sao Paulo.

eras.title: Seventeen years on
eras.text: In the long quiet, Ocampo made records with the Effects and Molter launched Whisper States. Then the three of them booked a Faraquet tour, and most of the dates sold out.

years.cap: Boswell, Ocampo and Molter at the Black Cat, Washington, DC, July 2025
yt: Cut Self Not at the Black Cat, July 2025
years.h: Faraquet plays its first show in 17 years at the Black Cat
years.p: The comeback opens at D.C.'s Black Cat on July 25, then sells out an early and a late show at Philadelphia's Phila MOCA before TV Eye in Ridgewood, Queens.
years.xp: Faraquet announced the shows in April. [[SAVAK|798aac2b-e30f-457a-a082-2826d8a5c533]] supported on the July Mid-Atlantic dates, and Cut Self Not was in the Black Cat set. The TV Eye show on July 27 sold out too.

yt: Live at Zebulon, Los Angeles, Sept 7, 2025
years.h: Zebulon in Los Angeles sells out, then Japan takes six nights
years.p: After Los Angeles on September 7, Faraquet plays Tokyo, Nara, Osaka and Nagoya, then closes with two sold-out nights at Tokyo's Fever.
years.xp: Dischord's list has Nine Spices in Tokyo (September 11, sold out), Neverland in Nara, Conpass in Osaka, Stiff Slack in Nagoya (sold out), then Fever on September 15 and 16, both sold out.
